newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Some wage demands would press rates - Australia govt.
newsitem.headline: Some wage demands would press rates - Australia govt.

text.p: Australian Workplace Relations Minister Peter Reith said on Tuesday some demands for wage increases would push wages growth above Reserve Bank targets and would not be good for interest rates.

"There are some pressures in some industries which would...if the demands were fully met would see relatively significant wage outcomes over and above the rates set by the Reserve Bank and that would not be good for interest rates, it would not be good for Australia's otherwise very good record in recent times on inflation," Reith told reporters.
Reith said latest official data on wages growth were "within certain reasonable bounds as far as the levels established or set by the Reserve Bank".
"To that extent, we have seen some relatively benign developments on the wages front over the last 12 months, but that is not in any sense to encourage any complacency on the wages front," he said.
